guideTitle: 5 Best Saker Handheld Steam Cleaners in 2026
metaDescription: Five Saker and SakerPlus handheld steamers compared on heat-up speed, tank size, hose reach and steam control to help you pick the right model for your home.
introParagraphs: Saker and SakerPlus sell a crowded set of near-identical handheld steam cleaners, and the listings lean on similar phrases, which makes it hard to see what actually separates one from another. The real differences are heat-up time, tank size, how steam is adjusted and how much hose and cord you get, and those differences change how the tool feels in a kitchen, bathroom or car.

We evaluated five Saker-branded models based on product specs and buyer feedback, leaving out near-duplicate listings of the same unit and every non-Saker alternative. The lineup runs from a 1.89 lb EverSteam that heats in about 15 seconds to a 2500W model with a 34 ounce tank, a 79 inch hose model, a 1.2 L six-level unit and a pressurized 4 lb pick with a classic 3 minute warm-up.
Use the picks below as a starting point, then work through the buying criteria and decision tables to match a Saker model to your jobs.

products.name: SakerPlus EverSteam 1350W Instant-Heat Steam Cleaner
products.description:
The EverSteam is the lightest and most balanced Saker model, weighing about 1.89 lb with a 1350W heater that reaches steam in roughly 15 seconds. It has a detachable 400 ml tank, High and Low steam modes, and an LED temperature display that lets you check the heater status at a glance. The kit adds a straight nozzle, an angled nozzle, a round brush, an extension hose and a window squeegee.

The tradeoff is capacity and control. Two modes are simpler than the six levels on the SakerPlus 2500W, but they are also less precise, and a 400 ml tank is a fraction of the 1.2 L on the Saker 6-Level. You also need to switch off the steam output before detaching the tank to refill, which is safe but adds a step.

Ownership is easy, with a 9.8 ft cord that is shorter than the 74.8 inch plus 59 inch combination on the 2500W model but fine for a single room. It is the natural fit for anyone who dislikes heavy tools, since at 1.89 lb it weighs less than half of the 4 lb pressurized SakerPlus. A near-identical listing of the same EverSteam also exists, so you can safely choose either one.
products.bestFor: People who want a very light steamer that heats in seconds for frequent, short jobs.
pros: Weighs about 1.89 lb, the lightest Saker model in this lineup
Ready in roughly 15 seconds, so quick jobs stay quick and simple
Detachable 400 ml tank refills at the sink without lifting the body
LED temperature display shows heater status at a glance as you work
cons: The 400 ml tank is small next to the 1.2 L Saker 6-Level model
Only High and Low modes, so less fine control than six levels
You must switch off the steam before detaching the tank to refill

products.name: SakerPlus 2500W Handheld Steam Cleaner, 6 Levels
products.description:
The SakerPlus 2500W is the strongest and fastest-heating model here, with a 2500W heater that reaches steam in about 10 seconds. It has six adjustable steam levels, a 34 ounce water tank, a 74.8 inch power cord and a 59 inch steam hose. The kit includes multiple dedicated brush attachments aimed at sealed surfaces.

The big tank and six levels make it the best match for a long, mixed session, such as grout in the bathroom followed by sofa cushions at a lower setting. The compromise is size and weight, because a 34 ounce reservoir and a 2500W heater make it noticeably heavier than the 1.89 lb EverSteam. It also draws a lot of power, so avoid sharing an outlet with other appliances.

The cord and hose together give roughly 11 feet of working radius, which is better than the 9.8 ft cord alone on the EverSteam. Compared with the Saker 6-Level at 1.2 L and 15 seconds, this one heats faster and has a stronger heater, but it carries less water. A near-identical listing of the same 2500W unit exists, and it is the pick for a household that wants one steamer for everything.
products.bestFor: Long, mixed cleaning sessions that need fast heat-up, six steam levels and a big tank.
pros: The 2500W heater reaches usable steam in about 10 seconds flat
Six steam levels cover both delicate and sturdy sealed surfaces
34 oz tank supports long sessions with fewer stops to refill
A 74.8 in cord plus a 59 in hose gives a generous working radius
cons: Heavier and bulkier in hand than the 1.89 lb EverSteam model
A 2500W draw is best kept on its own outlet, away from other loads
Holds noticeably less water than the 1.2 L Saker 6-Level model

products.name: SakerPlus 1500W Handheld Steam Cleaner, Knob Control
products.description:
This SakerPlus model is built around its 79 inch steam hose, which has a protective fabric sleeve to cover the hot tube. A 1500W heater produces steam up to 221°F, and an adjustment knob controls how much steam is released. The kit includes nylon brushes, a brass brush, scrapers, an angled joint, a window attachment, towel covers and a spray nozzle.

The long hose is what sets it apart, because you can place the body on a counter or floor and still reach appliances, bathroom fixtures and the far side of a car interior. The knob is a more tactile control than the buttons on other models, though it offers continuous adjustment rather than clear numbered steps. The listing does not state a heat-up time or a tank size, which makes it harder to compare with the 15 second EverSteam or the 34 ounce 2500W.

The fabric sleeve is a thoughtful touch, since steam hoses get hot enough to be uncomfortable to brush against. It suits sealed tile, counters, sinks, stovetops, windows, curtains and bedding, according to the listing. Pick it if reach matters more than speed, and look at the Saker 6-Level if you want a bigger, clearly labeled tank.
products.bestFor: Cleaning appliances, bathroom fixtures and car interiors where hose length beats portability.
pros: 79 in hose with a protective fabric sleeve is the longest listed here
Adjustment knob lets you trim steam release to the surface at hand
Kit adds a brass brush, scrapers, towel covers and a spray nozzle
The 1500W heater is a step above the EverSteam's 1350W heater
cons: The listing gives no heat-up time to compare with other models
No tank size is stated, so run time per fill is unknown to you
Knob adjustment is less repeatable than numbered steam levels

products.name: Saker 6-Level Handheld Steam Cleaner, 1.2 L Tank
products.description:
The Saker 6-Level carries a 1.2 L transparent water tank, the largest listed here, and heats in about 15 seconds to steam of up to 221°F. It offers six adjustable levels, from gentle steam for delicate fabrics to a strong blast for tile gaps. A flexible hose and extended power cord let you reach under furniture and into car interiors.

The clear tank is a practical feature, since you can see how much water is left without guessing, and it supports whole-home sessions or a car finish. The compromise is that the listing does not give exact figures for weight, cord length or wattage, so you cannot compare handling directly with the 1.89 lb EverSteam. It is also a tank-heavy body, which will feel heavier in hand than a 400 ml unit.

In use, six levels give you the same fine control as the 2500W, but with a bigger reservoir and a slightly longer wait of 15 seconds against 10. The accessory kit covers tiles, grout lines, windows, cushions and pet areas. It is a good middle path for people who want control and capacity without paying for the 2500W's raw power.
products.bestFor: Whole-home sessions where a large clear tank and six steam levels matter more than low weight.
pros: The 1.2 L transparent tank shows water level and lasts a long session
Six steam levels from gentle fabric steam to strong tile blasts
Heats in about 15 seconds, which is quick for a tank this large
Flexible hose and extended cord reach under furniture and in cars
cons: The listing gives no weight, wattage or cord length figures to use
Larger tank makes the body heavier than the 400 ml EverSteam
Heats in 15 seconds, slower than the SakerPlus 2500W at 10 seconds

products.name: SakerPlus Handheld Pressurized Steam Cleaner, 9-Piece
products.description:
The pressurized SakerPlus is the most traditional design in the group, with a 3.5 bar high-pressure boiler that heats in about 3 minutes and produces 230°F steam for 9 to 10 minutes. It holds a 380 ml tank and weighs about 4 lb, and the 9-piece kit includes a nozzle head, an angled nozzle, a brush head, an extension hose, a cloth cover and a window wiper, among others. The listing also mentions multiple safety features.

It is the slowest to heat and the heaviest, at roughly 4 lb against the 1.89 lb EverSteam, and the 9 to 10 minute steam window is shorter than most rivals. A fixed output means there are no steam levels, so delicate surfaces need a cloth and a steady hand. The listing also warns to fill the tank to the right level to prevent water leakage, which is a habit worth building.

What it offers is a simple, no-display machine with a listed 3.5 bar boiler. That makes it a fit for kitchen grease and tile grout where you want a forceful jet. For anyone who wants flexibility or speed, the EverSteam or the Saker 6-Level is the better pick.
products.bestFor: Occasional tile, grout and grease jobs where a forceful fixed jet is enough and speed is not critical.
pros: 3.5 bar boiler delivers a forceful jet for grease and grout lines
Steam at 230°F is hotter than the 221°F on two other Saker models
The 9-piece kit adds a cloth cover, extension hose and window wiper
Safety features are listed, and the 380 ml tank is easy to fill
cons: Heats in about 3 minutes, the slowest of the five Saker models
Weighs about 4 lb, which is over twice the 1.89 lb EverSteam
Steam lasts only 9 to 10 minutes and has no adjustable levels

buyingCriteria.explanation: Heat-up decides how often you will actually grab the tool. The SakerPlus 2500W lists about 10 seconds, the EverSteam and Saker 6-Level list about 15, and the pressurized SakerPlus needs about 3 minutes. For a household that steams something every week, anything under 30 seconds changes habits, while a 3 minute wait suits a planned session. The 1500W knob model gives no figure, so check the listing before you buy.

Saker uses four control styles, which is more variety than most brands. The SakerPlus 2500W and Saker 6-Level offer six numbered levels, the EverSteam offers High and Low with an LED display, the 1500W model uses a knob, and the pressurized unit has a single output. Six levels suit mixed surfaces, two modes suit simple households, and a single output suits hard, sealed tile only. If you steam fabrics, avoid the single-output model.

A steamer is held out in front of you, so weight adds up quickly. The EverSteam is listed at about 1.89 lb and the pressurized SakerPlus at about 4 lb, which is more than double. The 2500W and 1.2 L models carry bigger tanks and are heavier than the EverSteam, though the listing does not give numbers for them. If you have limited grip strength, choose the lightest option and refill more often.

Small tanks mean light bodies and frequent refills, while large tanks give long sessions and extra weight. The EverSteam holds 400 ml, the pressurized SakerPlus 380 ml for 9 to 10 minutes, the 2500W holds 34 ounces and the Saker 6-Level holds 1.2 L. If your longest job is a full bathroom, aim for at least 34 ounces. For short sink and stovetop jobs, 400 ml is enough.

Reach decides how often you move the unit. The 1500W model offers a 79 inch hose with a fabric sleeve, the 2500W offers a 74.8 inch cord and 59 inch hose, and the EverSteam has a 9.8 ft cord. Add cord and hose to estimate your working radius, and avoid extension cords near water. If you plan on cars or stairs, prefer a long hose over a long cord.

Steam above 220°F can burn, so look for safety features and follow the usual rules. The pressurized SakerPlus lists multiple safety features, and the EverSteam adds an LED display for heater status. Use steam only on sealed surfaces, test hidden spots on fabrics, and never aim steam at people or pets. Wipe loosened grime immediately so it does not resettle, and empty the tank after use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat-up speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the stated time to usable steam for each Saker model. The SakerPlus 2500W leads at about 10 seconds, the EverSteam and Saker 6-Level follow at about 15, and the pressurized SakerPlus trails at about 3 minutes. The 1500W knob model does not state a figure, so it was scored cautiously.

howWeEvaluated.title: Steam control
howWeEvaluated.description: Adjustability matters for mixed surfaces, so we counted the number of levels and how they are set. The SakerPlus 2500W and Saker 6-Level lead with six levels, the EverSteam gives two modes with a display, and the 1500W model has a knob. The pressurized SakerPlus has a single output.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at listed weight, tank size and whether the tank is removable. The EverSteam is the lightest at about 1.89 lb with a detachable 400 ml tank, and the pressurized SakerPlus is the heaviest at about 4 lb. Handling matters because tired hands often mean uneven results.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and accessories
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cord length, hose length and the kit. The 1500W model leads on hose at 79 inches, the 2500W offers a 74.8 inch cord and 59 inch hose, and the pressurized SakerPlus offers a 9-piece kit. Accessory counts only helped when the tools suit the job.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed tank size against body weight and heat-up. The Saker 6-Level at 1.2 L and the 2500W at 34 oz lead on capacity, while the EverSteam is the most balanced for its weight. Neither of the larger-tank models is as light as the 1.89 lb EverSteam, so the right ranking depends on your priorities.

faq.q: What is the difference between Saker and SakerPlus?
faq.a: The listings use both names, and they appear to be the same family sold under slightly different brand wording. Models differ in wattage, tank size, hose and control style, so compare those rather than the name. In this guide the Saker 6-Level is the one listed under the plain Saker brand.

faq.q: Which Saker model heats up fastest?
faq.a: The SakerPlus 2500W lists about 10 seconds, ahead of the EverSteam and Saker 6-Level at about 15 seconds. The pressurized SakerPlus needs about 3 minutes. The 1500W knob model does not list a heat-up time, so assume it is somewhere in between until you check.

Yes. The EverSteam and the 2500W model each appear under two similar listings with identical specs. We treated each pair as one product. Pick whichever listing has the more convenient shipping or return terms.

Mineral scale is the main durability problem for any steamer, and distilled or demineralized water slows it. Some manuals say tap water can void guarantees, so check yours. The pressurized SakerPlus listing also warns to fill the tank only to the stated level to avoid leakage. Empty the tank after each session.

faq.q: Is a bigger wattage always better?
faq.a: No. Wattage mostly affects how fast the unit heats and recovers, and the 2500W model heats in about 10 seconds against the EverSteam's 15 seconds at 1350W. Steam pressure, tank size and control matter just as much in daily use. A higher wattage also means more power draw and often more weight.

faq.q: Is steam safe on every surface?
faq.a: No. Steam is best on sealed tile, grout, sinks, stovetops and many car surfaces. Avoid unsealed wood, waxed finishes, delicate paint, electronics and cold glass, and test a hidden spot on fabrics first. The listings for the Saker models themselves refer to suitable sealed surfaces.

For many jobs, steam softens grease and soap scum so a microfiber cloth lifts it without sprays. Wipe immediately so loosened soil does not resettle. Treat steam as a cleaning aid, not a medical guarantee of sanitizing. Heavy mold or baked-on residue may still need additional work.
